title: Why Does the Slope Definition of $e$ Work?: A Self-Contained Exploration After Real Analysis
summary: Euler's number $e$ is often introduced through compound interest, an infinite series, an area, or the slope of an exponential function. The last viewpoint is especially attractive: choose the base $b\in (2,3)$ so that the graph of $y=b^x$ has tangent slope $1$ at $(0,1)$. However, a curious student may raise several questions that a brief introduction necessarily leaves implicit. What does $b^x$ mean when $x$ is irrational? Why is $b^x$ differentiable at $x = 0$?
